purpose: Dependency bootstrap, seed and reproducibility contract.
Establish what the simulator actually produces before interpreting any downstream signal: schema, missingness, identifiers, split boundaries, class balance and known generator artifacts.
Characterize the marginal distributions of amount, time, category, demographics and geography, and quantify how far fraud separates from genuine activity on each axis.
Test whether risk concentrates in combinations of category, time, geography and cardholder behavior, and measure the money exposure behind transaction counts.
Determine whether fraud is temporally clustered and how volume, seasonality and structural breaks evolve across the 2019–2020 observation window.
Test whether fraud separates without labels using embeddings, clustering and anomaly detection, and document the limits of visual separability.
Replace significance-only claims with effect sizes, bootstrap intervals, multiple-testing correction and inference that respects the card-level repeated measures.
Build leak-aware behavioral features and test whether velocity, cohorts, hazards, hierarchical shrinkage and encoding choices add interpretable signal.
Measure leak-free predictive performance, diagnose train→test transfer, calibrate probabilities and translate scores into review-budget economics.
Compile the graded findings ledger, figure/table index, reproducibility checklist and output bundle, and verify the expected phase-8 artifacts exist.
